properties.title: Ultrasound Operator Guidance Using World Modeling and Retrieval Based Action Planning

membership.reason: Learned V-JEPA 2.1 latent state space (shaped by forward/inverse dynamics) coupled with a nonparametric retrieval-induced latent transition operator Gamma_D and receding-horizon planner (H=6) for 6-DoF carotid ultrasound guidance.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L4 decision-coupled world model (WT_ACQUISITION); note transition operator at inference is nonparametric retrieval.

properties.backbone: V-JEPA 2.1 encoder f_theta + nonparametric retrieval-induced transition operator Gamma_D + receding-horizon tree planner (H=6)

properties.flow: 4-frame live US clip -> V-JEPA 2.1 encoder f_theta -> Retrieval-induced H=6 tree search over recorded transitions -> 6-DoF probe guidance instruction -> Receding-horizon replanning

properties.purpose: Real-time pose-sensor-free 6-DoF operator guidance for carotid ultrasound standard views.
properties.environment: Retrospective closed-loop replay (13 test volunteers) + prospective real-time CPU study on unseen volunteers

properties.participant_description: Three previously unseen healthy volunteers scanned live by a single blinded human operator (randomized between proposed planner and Cardiac Copilot-inspired baseline, ~12 min per volunteer; TU/e ethical review board approved with informed consent).
properties.outcome_summary: Real-time CPU execution (distilled V-JEPA 2.1, H=3) reached 83% target-view reachability versus 72% for Cardiac Copilot-inspired baseline across six standard carotid views.

Transition structure is learned from data: V-JEPA 2.1 latent space f_theta is shaped by forward-dynamics and inverse-dynamics heads during training (Section III-C, p.5), and the nonparametric retrieval-induced latent transition operator Gamma_D (Section III-D.1, pp.5-6) maps latent states to action-successor pairs via nearest-neighbor retrieval over learned embeddings and empirically recorded 6-DoF transitions (note in limitations: inference-time transitions are nonparametric retrieval rather than a parametric dynamics rollout network).
Each retrieved transition pairs a recorded 6-DoF action a_{i,Delta} with successor latent z_{j*}.
Evaluates H=6 multi-step planning trajectories in closed-loop retrospective replay.
Uses retrieval-induced world model transitions for multi-step action planning.

Lane-pruned branching receding-horizon tree search (K=10 neighbors, N_lane=5, H=6 retrospective / H=3 prospective CPU) is evaluated against UltraSeP-style and Cardiac Copilot-style baselines in retrospective closed-loop replay (86% vs 52%/43%, p.8), horizon/cost/database-retrieval ablations (Tables III-V, pp.9-10), and a blinded prospective volunteer study (83% vs 72%, pp.9-10).
Issues only the first action a^(1)(tau*) and replans upon each new ultrasound observation.
86% target-view reachability in retrospective closed-loop episodes (vs 52%/43%) and 83% in prospective unseen-volunteer CPU study.

Prospective real-time CPU feasibility study on unseen human volunteers (83% reachability).

evidence_fragments.content: Applied to carotid ultrasound, the proposed planner reaches the target view in 86% of retrospective closed-loop episodes, versus 52% and 43% for representative baselines, outperforming both on every target view, including the challenging longitudinal internal and external carotid artery views. A prospective feasibility study on unseen volunteers, run in real time on a CPU using distillation, reaches 83% target-view reachability.

Fig. 2. Visual overview of the ultrasound world model and planning in its latent space. A) Training sequences are encoded into latent states using the learned encoder f θ, based purely on the visual ultrasound frames; each training frame additionally has a ground-truth recorded pose, used to calculate actions between training frames. B) The live imaging sequence is encoded with the same encoder f θ. Many candidate trajectories are then randomly sampled by alternating between retrieval hops and within-trajectory hops.

48 recorded trajectories, each from a different volunteer who gave informed consent, totaling 247,827 ultrasound frames. Data were partitioned at the subject level into training (n = 31), validation (n = 4), and test (n = 13) sets

locator.section_or_table: Section III-C Latent ultrasound world modeling

evidence_fragments.content: All three heads serve only to shape the representation during training; none of their predictions are used afterward. In particular, planning remains fully nonparametric and relies exclusively on the recorded actions stored in the transition database (Eq. 12), never on g actionθ or g forwardθ predictions, and the view probabilities used for goal specification come instead from a separate, dedicated module, described next.

Following a receding-horizon strategy, only the first action of the selected trajectory is communicated to the user, at = a (1)(τ ⋆).(22) A new ultrasound observation is then acquired, and the complete planning procedure is repeated.

style guidance and 43% for Cardiac Copilot-style guidance. Random-frame initialization degrades success less for the proposed method than for the baselines, indicating lower sensitivity to the starting location.

We performed a prospective feasibility study on three previously unseen healthy volunteers. The examinations were performed by the same operator who acquired the retrospective dataset. The navigation software was executed entirely on a standard CPU using a distilled version of the V-JEPA 2.1 model, with a planning horizon of three, a compromise between navigation performance and computational efficiency that enables real-time operation without GPU acceleration.

capability_assessments.rationale: Receding-horizon tree planner (H=6) over retrieval-induced transitions in a learned V-JEPA 2.1 latent space, evaluated in closed-loop retrospective replay (86%) and prospective volunteer study (83%).

scope.note: R2 retrospective closed-loop replay on 13 test volunteers; R4 prospective real-time CPU feasibility study on unseen healthy volunteers.

limitations: Inference-time transition operator is nonparametric retrieval over recorded trajectories rather than a parametric generative dynamics model.
Prospective feasibility study was limited to three healthy volunteers and a single operator (no patients with carotid pathology and no multi-operator/novice evaluation).

legacy_cells.O: Carotid ultrasound views: common carotid artery, bulb, bifurcation, internal carotid artery, and external carotid artery
legacy_cells.S: Can retrieval-based multi-step planning guide an operator's probe to a target carotid ultrasound view?
legacy_cells.T: Retrospective dataset: 48 volunteers, one trajectory per volunteer; prospective feasibility study: three previously unseen healthy volunteers.
legacy_cells.U: Human ultrasound operator, including a less-trained user
legacy_cells.V: Which relative probe motion to communicate next to guide the operator toward the target view
legacy_cells.AI: B-mode ultrasound video clips (four consecutive frames); tracked six-degree-of-freedom probe poses in training acquisitions to derive recorded relative motions (pose sensing is not used at deployment)
legacy_cells.AJ: Fine-tuned V-JEPA 2.1 backbone with attentive pooling; prospective distilled model uses a MobileNetV3-Small image encoder and a small transformer.
legacy_cells.BD: Relative six-degree-of-freedom probe motion: translation in millimeters and pitch, roll, and yaw in degrees
legacy_cells.BI: Retrieval-induced latent transition model (no separate proper name stated)
legacy_cells.BS: Retrieved future latent states and the corresponding recorded relative probe motions; the next observation is acquired from the live feed rather than generated.
legacy_cells.BU: Trajectory cost balances target-view likelihood, progress toward the target, and smooth probe motion, including penalties for changes in direction and reversal across replanning steps.
legacy_cells.CD: Eight planning steps (maximum horizon in the reported horizon sweep)
legacy_cells.CI: Six steps in retrospective evaluation; three steps in the prospective feasibility study
legacy_cells.DN: Self-collected tracked carotid ultrasound acquisitions; prospective unseen-volunteer feasibility acquisitions
legacy_cells.DQ: 48 retrospective volunteers; 3 previously unseen healthy volunteers in prospective feasibility
legacy_cells.EC: Retrospective closed-loop target reachability 86%, versus 52% and 43% for baselines; prospective three-volunteer study: 83% versus 72% for Cardiac Copilot-inspired guidance. These are acquisition-feasibility outcomes, not patient health benefits.
legacy_cells.EG: Prospective distilled model runs in real time entirely on a standard CPU; MobileNetV3-Small encoder and small transformer, horizon three.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): Applied to carotid ultrasound, the proposed planner reaches the target view in 86% of retrospective closed-loop episodes, versus 52% and 43% for representative baselines, outperforming both on every target view, including the challenging longitudinal internal and external carotid artery views. A prospective feasibility study on unseen volunteers, run in real time on a CPU using distillation, reaches 83% target-view reachability.
legacy_cells.FO: Single acquisition operator, single ultrasound system and three healthy prospective volunteers limit generalization; view ambiguity and guidance communication remain challenges.
legacy_cells.FP: Include multiple operators including novices, evaluate scanner robustness, improve intuitive communication of corrective probe motions, and examine other ultrasound applications.
legacy_cells.FR: Prospective feasibility in three healthy volunteers with the same experienced acquisition operator; no novice/multisite trial, patient-outcome benefit or regulated clinical deployment is demonstrated.
